title: French high school students protest conditions, block schools nationwide
seoTitle: Lens student protests over school conditions

tea.why: Students are protesting teacher absences, poor classroom conditions, overloaded timetables, and long school days in an overcrowded education system.
tea.want: Protesters are demanding better classroom conditions, more staff, and increased resources for the education system.
tea.changed: Oct 5: A 15-year-old in Lens lost a hand after a police-fired sting-ball grenade exploded during clashes.

summary: Nationwide student protests in France began around September 21, initially at a high school near Paris, in support of striking teachers. The demonstrations quickly spread, with students expressing grievances over teacher absences, poor classroom conditions, overcrowded schools, and long school days. On October 5, over 500 high schools were disrupted or closed. During clashes in Lens, a 15-year-old lost a hand after picking up a police-fired sting-ball grenade. The government has attempted to address the issues but has also accused hard-left activists of co-opting the movement. Police have taken over 5,000 people into custody, and reports indicate 215 students and 715 police officers have been injured.
response: The government has sought to address student grievances, but has also accused hard-left activists of hijacking the movement. Police have taken more than 5,000 people into custody, most of whom are minors. Critics have accused the police of a heavy-handed response.

arrests.text: More than 5,000 people have been taken into police custody

injuries.text: The government noted that the ongoing unrest has left 215 students and 715 police officers injured

updates.text: Student protests began at Saint-Exupéry high school near Paris, supporting striking teachers over staff and resource shortages.
Protesters hurled firecrackers at riot police in Pantin, near Paris.
Over 500 high schools were shut down or partially disrupted nationwide as student unrest intensified.
A 15-year-old in Lens lost a hand when a police-fired sting-ball grenade exploded.
Demonstrators were preparing for further nationwide protests, referred to as 'Act III'.
